# v1.0.0 — a stable API, a new name, and a decoder that survives hostile input

The API stops changing here. What that promise covers is written down in the
[compatibility policy](https://github.com/wirunrom/barqr/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#compatibility).

**The package moved to `barqr`.** `@wirunrom/hqr-generate` is deprecated;
its last release is 0.6.0. See
[MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/wirunrom/barqr/blob/v1.0.0/MIGRATION.md)
— for most code the whole change is the import path.

| | 0.6.0 | 1.0.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package | `@wirunrom/hqr-generate` | **`barqr`** |
| Frameworks | React | React **and Vue / Nuxt** |
| Decoding a 1.2 MB crafted PNG | 976 MB, 2.2 s | **refused in <1 ms** |
| Reachable panic in the decoder | yes | **fixed** |
| Tests | 37 Rust · 45 package · 15 browser (manual) | 37 · 45 · **15 headless in CI** |
| CI | 2 platforms | **3 platforms + MSRV + weekly fuzzing** |

## 🔒 Security

Two real vulnerabilities, both found while preparing this release, both
reachable from `decode` with input a user could supply.

**Unbounded allocation from a small file.** A compressed image describes a
canvas rather than containing one. A 1.2 MB PNG declaring 16000×16000 made the
decoder allocate **976 MB** and burn 2.2 s of CPU before concluding there was no
QR code — roughly an 800× amplification. `image`'s own `max_alloc` did not help,
because the largest allocation was this crate's `to_rgba8()` call, downstream of
that accounting. Dimensions are now checked against the header before any pixels
are read; over 40 megapixels is refused with `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`, allocating
nothing.

**A reachable panic.** Fuzzing produced RGBA input that panicked inside
`rqrr` 0.7: `Perspective::map` asserts its result fits in an `i32`, but that
value is computed from image data, and a degenerate transform drives it to
infinity or NaN. This matters more than an ordinary dependency bug, because
`wasm32-unknown-unknown` has `panic-strategy: abort` — a panic in the decode
path takes the whole WASM instance with it and **cannot be caught**. One crafted
image would end QR decoding for the life of a page, or of a server request.
Fixed by moving to `rqrr` 0.10; the input is kept as a regression test.

Fuzzing is now permanent: two `cargo-fuzz` targets, a seed corpus generated from
real encoder output, and a weekly CI run.

## ✨ Vue and Nuxt

`barqr/vue` ships the same five composables the React layer exposes.
Values, refs and getters are all accepted; everything is released on scope
disposal.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQr } from "barqr/vue";
const { src } = useQr(() => props.url, { size: 320 });
</script>
```

The SSR guard is the substance here. `watchEffect` runs during server rendering
while React's `useEffect` does not, so an unguarded composable would try to
`fetch()` the WASM binary mid-render and take down every Nuxt page using it.
Generation is deferred to the client; for QR codes in the server-rendered HTML,
call the synchronous Node API from a server route.

Verified against Nuxt 4.5 with **no bundler configuration** — no
`nitro.externals`, no `build.transpile`. `tests/nuxt-app/nuxt.config.ts` is
empty on purpose.

## 💥 Breaking

- **The package name.** See MIGRATION.md.
- **The snake_case aliases are gone** — `generate_png`, `generate_svg`,
  `generate_modules`. Use the camelCase names.
- **Images over 40 megapixels are refused** with `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`.
- **Rust MSRV is 1.88**, corrected from a declared 1.85 that was never true:
  `image` has required 1.88 for some time, so `--features decode` could not have
  built there. The new CI job caught it on its first run.
- **Rust:** error enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`; `render_svg(&QrBitmap)` is
  removed — it emitted one `<rect>` per module, 143 KB against 5.2 KB.

Everything else is unchanged: all eight functions, every option, all five React
hooks.

## 🧪 Testing

- **37 Rust tests** — sizing, 1-bit scanline clearing against a naive reference,
  logo budgets, and generate→decode round trips across every ECC level, size,
  margin and a Thai/Japanese/emoji payload set.
- **45 package tests** — the shipped entry points, `exports` resolution, the
  ESM/CJS boundary, every payload builder including PromptPay's TLV structure
  and CRC, and Vue SSR through `vue/server-renderer`.
- **15 browser tests, now headless in CI** — WASM over HTTP, canvas round trips,
  object-URL lifetimes, the scanner against a canvas-backed `MediaStream`, and
  all five Vue composables in a mounted app.
- **Two framework fixtures** that install the packed tarball and import by
  package name: `tests/my-app` (Next.js) and `tests/nuxt-app` (Nuxt). Between
  them they have caught three bugs no unit test could see.
- CI on Linux, macOS and Windows, at the declared MSRV, with a bundle size
  budget that fails the build.

## Still verified by hand, not by CI

**PromptPay** payloads are checked for TLV structure and against the standard
CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE vector, and they round-trip through the decoder — but no
automated test can put one in front of a real banking app. Confirm before taking
payments. The same goes for the **camera scanner** on physical hardware: it is
tested against a canvas-backed `MediaStream`, which exercises every line of the
pump, but not a real sensor.
